title: Come, Thou All-inspiring Spirit
description: Come, Thou All-inspiring Spirit in Tonic Solfa to LUX EOI, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 530.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to LUX EOI; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, thou all in-spir-ing Spir-it, In-to ev-ery long-ing heart! Bought for us by Je-su's mer-it, Now thy bliss-ful self im-part; Sign our un-con-test-ed par-don, Wash us in th'a-ton-ing blood! Make our hearts a wa-tered gar-den; Fill our spot-less souls with God.

lines: Bought for us by Jesu's merit,
Wash us in the atoning blood!
Make our hearts a watered garden;
Fill our spotless souls with God.
If thou gav'st the enlarged desire,
Which for thee we ever feel,
Seal us heirs of full salvation,
Till for all thy glory meet,
Keep us from the world unspotted,
Fixed to live and die for thee.
Lord, we will not let thee go,
Till thou all thy mind declare,
All thy grace on us bestow;
Peace, the seal of sin forgiven,
All thou hast, and all thou art!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to LUX EOI by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
